ELI5: why do medications have side effects?

Because the body is complex.

Complex doesn't mean "very complicated", it means there are different tiers of systems at work.

With medicine, we can't target a single thing yet, so the effect that the medicine has is applied to multiple systems in the body. If your problem is with a single system that is out of whack, you need to effect multiple systems to treat it. If these systems don't need to be treated, they are thrown out of whack by what fixed the first system, and you get side effects.
my doctor says that it's a mistake to call them side effects, because for the most part they are direct effects of the drugs you're taking.
But that would be called being honest. And that's bad marketing.

When a medication goes into your body, it binds to a receptor. Many parts of your body share the same kind of receptor. For example, a person with heart problems may be prescribed a non-selective beta blocker (blocks beta receptors) to control it. However, other organs like the lungs, eyes, blood vessels, and stomach also contain beta receptors. So while this medicine is helping the heart function normally, it may affect those other organs, so they don't feel normal (side effects).
